title: Copilot review findings lead with the fix, then the why
answers: How should Copilot code review comments be formatted in this repo?
What sections must a review finding have in code-review.instructions.md?
Why does the review comment start with the recommended fix instead of the problem?
Where is the review comment format for Copilot defined?
body:
Convention: when a review finding has a recommended fix, write it as two short bold-labelled sections, in this order.
- "**🔧 Fix:**" comes first and states the recommended change, with only the detail needed to implement it.
- "**💡 Why:**" follows and states the trigger and the concrete consequence that make the fix necessary.
- The format is defined in the "## Review Comment Format" section of .github/instructions/code-review.instructions.md.
- Keep the two labels and their order if you edit that section; the Copilot reviewer reads this file.
applies: Only for Copilot/agent code review output in this repository, as set by .github/instructions/code-review.instructions.md; not for human review comments or general docs.
says: Copilot code review comments should show the recommended fix before explaining the reason.
Automated pull request review feedback displays the background explanation ahead of the required change.
Format reviewer bot comments with the concrete solution first followed by the rationale.
The automated reviewer suggestions should put actionable code changes ahead of explanations.
search: Copilot review findings with recommended fixes must present two bold-labelled sections starting with '**🔧 Fix:**' followed by '**💡 Why:**'. The fix section states the recommended change with minimal implementation detail, while the why section describes the trigger and concrete consequences requiring the change. Defined in the '## Review Comment Format' section of .github/instructions/code-review.instructions.md, this convention applies strictly to Copilot and agent review comments rather than human reviews or general documentation.
